briefs.working_title: The Gap Under Your Door Is How Ants and Roaches Get Into Bradenton Homes — A 20-Minute Fix
secondary_kws: seal gap under exterior door bugs
how do ants get in under the door
briefs.thesis: A daylight gap under an exterior door is the single most common entry point a technician finds on a Bradenton pest inspection, and a homeowner can close it with an adjustable door sweep in an afternoon — which reduces pressure but does not replace treatment for an active colony.
outline: The flashlight test: why you can see daylight under the door and what walks through that gap (ants, roaches, silverfish, anoles)
Why Bradenton homes get it worse: slab foundations, sun-warped garage-side doors, and year-round insect pressure (per UF/IFAS)
Measure the gap first: thresholds, uneven slabs, and why the cheap flat sweeps fail on Florida doors
Installing an adjustable double-bubble door sweep step by step (this is where the product recommendation belongs — the adjustable sweep is the tool for uneven gaps)
What a door sweep will NOT fix: an established ant colony, roaches already inside the wall voids, and the other entry points a professional inspection checks
When to call Waves: signs the problem is bigger than the gap
sources: UF/IFAS EDIS for the exclusion and household-pest entry claims (search 'exclusion' and the specific pest); cite the publication you actually used.
verify_notes: Verify every pest-behavior claim (which pests enter under doors, why) against a UF/IFAS EDIS publication; omit any claim you cannot source.
Do not claim the sweep 'keeps pests out' — it reduces one entry point; say so plainly.
No pesticide is recommended in this post; do not add one.

briefs.working_title: Weep Holes, Pipe Gaps and Roof-Line Openings: Copper Mesh Exclusion for Sarasota Homes
briefs.thesis: Sarasota block-and-stucco homes are full of small openings that must stay open for drainage (weep holes) or were never sealed (pipe and cable penetrations), and copper mesh is the exclusion material that closes them to rodents and roaches without trapping moisture or rusting.
outline: Where the openings are: block weep holes, A/C line sets, hose bibs, cable and gas penetrations, soffit and fascia gaps
Why weep holes must NOT be caulked shut (moisture and drainage in Sarasota's stucco-over-block construction) — exclusion has to breathe
Copper mesh vs steel wool vs foam: why steel wool rusts and stains and foam gets chewed (per UF/IFAS exclusion guidance)
How to stuff and seat copper mesh in a weep hole and around a pipe (this is where the product recommendation belongs)
The walk-around inspection order: ground level, then knee height, then the roof line
What exclusion does not solve: rodents already nesting in the attic, and roaches established indoors — when to call Waves

briefs.working_title: Stop Guessing: A Rain Gauge Is the First Tool a Venice Lawn Needs Before You Touch the Irrigation Timer
secondary_kws: how much rain did my lawn get
briefs.thesis: Most Venice lawn problems the crew diagnoses in the wet season trace back to irrigation running on top of rain, and the cheapest correction is knowing the actual rainfall at the house — a glass rain gauge, read after each storm, before deciding whether the zones run.
outline: The wet-season trap: afternoon storms plus a timer that never adjusts, and what that does to St. Augustine and zoysia turf (fungus, shallow roots, chinch-bug stress) per UF/IFAS
Why the phone weather app is wrong for your yard: Venice storms are hyper-local
Reading rainfall at the house: where to mount a rain gauge, how to read it, and the weekly total UF/IFAS recommends for established turf
The simple rule: when the gauge shows the week's water, skip the zones (this is where the product recommendation belongs)
Sarasota County and Venice watering-day rules and rain-sensor requirements — verify current rules before stating them

briefs.working_title: Is Your Lakewood Ranch Lawn Overwatered? A Soil Moisture Meter Answers in Ten Seconds
briefs.primary_kw: soil moisture meter lawn lakewood ranch
briefs.thesis: Overwatering causes more Lakewood Ranch lawn problems than drought does — fungus, shallow roots, and grub-friendly turf — and a battery-free soil moisture probe read at root depth is the fastest way a homeowner can tell whether the problem is water before assuming it is pests.
outline: Overwatered vs underwatered: why the symptoms look alike (yellowing, thin patches, footprints that stay) and why guessing costs a season
What root-depth moisture actually tells you in Lakewood Ranch's sandy, fast-draining soils (per UF/IFAS)
How to probe: depth, how many spots per zone, and reading the scale before and after an irrigation cycle (this is where the product recommendation belongs)
Turning readings into a schedule: watering deeper and less often, and matching the timer to the readings, not the calendar
The diseases and pests that ride on overwatering — dollar spot, brown patch, grubs — and the point where a schedule fix is no longer enough
When to call Waves for a lawn program
sources: UF/IFAS EDIS for turf watering depth/frequency, overwatering symptoms, and the disease/pest claims; cite the publication you actually used.
verify_notes: Verify every disease, pest, and soil claim against UF/IFAS; omit anything unsourced.
Do not attribute a specific moisture-scale number to 'correct' — describe the reading relative to the meter's own scale and root depth.

briefs.working_title: Dry Spots in a Parrish Lawn: Run a Catch-Cup Sprinkler Audit Before Blaming Pests
briefs.thesis: A recurring dry patch in a Parrish lawn is more often an irrigation coverage gap than a pest problem, and a 30-minute catch-cup audit — the same test a licensed irrigation auditor runs — shows exactly which zone and head is short before anyone reaches for a treatment.
outline: Dry spot or chinch bug? The look-alike problem in Parrish's newer subdivisions with builder-grade irrigation
What a catch-cup audit measures: application rate and distribution uniformity (per UF/IFAS)
Setting up the audit: cup grid spacing per zone, run time, and reading the cups (this is where the product recommendation belongs)
Reading the results: low-cup clusters mean a blocked or tilted head, mismatched nozzles, or pressure loss — the fixes in order of cost
Setting run times from the measured rate instead of the timer default, and Manatee County watering-day rules (verify the live page)
When the dry spot is not water: the signs that point to chinch bugs or grubs, and what a Waves lawn program does next
